trust_decision.summary: At admission of a ClusterLogForwarder CREATE or UPDATE in observability.openshift.io/v1, the requesting user (taken from the admission request UserInfo) must be allowed verb 'use' on the ServiceAccount named in spec.serviceAccount.name in the CLF's own namespace, decided by a SubjectAccessReview issued by the operator, for every CLF regardless of whether any output forwards the SA token.

landing_point.why: It is the only authorization-shaped code about the CLF's service account at the pinned commit: an SAR-driven check registered in the validator list (internal/validations/observability/validate.go:14-22); an engineer reading 'missing authorization in the Cluster Logging Operator' greps for 'authoriz' and lands here first.

fix_sites.entry_point: Admission webhook /validate-observability-openshift-io-v1-clusterlogforwarder on CREATE and UPDATE of clusterlogforwarders.observability.openshift.io/v1 (ValidateCreate and ValidateUpdate both call validateSAUsage)
operator manager startup: clfwebhook.SetupWebhookWithManager(mgr) registers the validator with the manager's webhook server (fix.diff:122-125); without it the validator is never invoked

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: fix.diff:122-125 (inserted at cmd/main.go:215; the shipped protection also needs config/webhook/manifests.yaml and the CSV webhookdefinitions at fix.diff:76-96)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The controller already runs an SAR-based authorization check on the CLF's service account (ValidatePermissions), and the SA token is only projected when an output asks for it, so SA usage can look already-authorized and harmless without a new admission check.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Cluster-admin/aggregated-role callers and users granted use through a group legitimately reference SAs without any named use Role; an over-broad fix that scans Role/RoleBinding objects for the use verb (or blocks openshift-*/kube-* namespaces) rejects them, whereas the project's own pattern is a SubjectAccessReview that honours wildcards, aggregation and groups.

O6_input_shapes: spec.serviceAccount.name non-empty: SAR 'use' on serviceaccounts in clf.Namespace is required
spec.serviceAccount.name empty: allowed by early return (fix.diff:424-427), even though the CRD marks the field required (api/observability/v1/clusterlogforwarder_types.go:76-89)
CREATE (ValidateCreate) and UPDATE (ValidateUpdate), with the old object ignored on update
requester identity shape: user, groups and UID are all copied into the SAR subject (fix.diff:437-441)
CLF with and without outputs[].authentication.token.from: serviceAccount: checked unconditionally (fix.diff:415-417)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second ServiceAccount-bearing field on the CLF spec, e.g. a per-output token serviceAccountName next to outputs[].authentication.token.from: serviceAccount
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the CRD already has a token-auth enum that is tied to the forwarder SA, so a maintainer adding per-output credentials would naturally add a name field there that reaches the same RBAC/token sink.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second SA-consuming branch beside NeedServiceAccountToken() that resolves a user-supplied SA name, mints its token secret and mounts it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this block already fetches the SA and creates <sa>-token; extending it for an output-specific SA is a one-line change a maintainer would plausibly make there instead of in a webhook.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: ReconcileServiceAccount accepting a caller-chosen SA name and creating it with the CLF owner reference/finalizers
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the function already conditionally creates an SA for a workload; relaxing the hardcoded name check is a small, tempting extension.

O9_family: CWE-862 missing authorization: caller-controlled ServiceAccount reference drives an operator-created workload and operator-written RBAC/SCC bindings (privilege escalation / SA impersonation)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25.0, toolchain go1.25.7 (go.mod:3-5); ginkgo/gomega; controller-runtime; no vendor directory
O10_build.project_tests: unit tests run offline via make test-unit (Makefile:235-239: go test -race ./api/... ./internal/...); no envtest in the tree; the same area is covered by internal/validations/observability/validate_permissions_test.go at the pinned commit; the fix adds internal/webhook/clusterlogforwarder_webhook_test.go (fake client + admission context) and a cluster-only e2e suite under test/e2e/collection/sa_authorization/

j.j_sites_touched: cmd/main.go, internal/webhook/clusterlogforwarder_webhook.go (plus config/webhook/*.yaml, config/default/*.yaml and bundle/manifests/cluster-logging.clusterserviceversion.yaml, which are not Go source)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Extend ValidatePermissions in internal/validations/observability (which already builds SubjectAccessReviews) to 'authorize' the SA, then discover the reconcile path has no requesting-user identity and either compare nothing or compare the SA to itself.

out_of_scope_notes: Adjacent but not this advisory's property: the operator also fetches caller-named Secrets (internal/controller/observability/clusterlogforwarder_controller.go:139-153) with its own privileges and embeds them into the generated collector config; a similar missing-authorization pattern on a different resource/verb - not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell in this session), so O4.repo_mb is null and the tiny_repo/giant_repo flags could not be evaluated; the tree is clearly not tiny (large test/, docs/ and API surface).
Webhook registration, the ValidatingWebhookConfiguration and SubjectAccessReview behaviour were verified by reading only; no cluster was run and nothing was built.
How hidden behavioural tests could drive the new webhook without pinning internal package/type names was not determined; the published fix's own tests are package-local (internal/webhook).

The published fix's ValidateUpdate ignores the old object, so any update of a CLF whose SA the editor cannot 'use' is rejected even when the SA is unchanged; whether a benchmark test treats that as intended or over-broad is unknown.
